answer: A loose kettle is a small thing until the water will not boil. Proof of coppersmith kettle via hammer dent tally is the coppersmith's proof: a kettle the coppersmith raises only after 14 dents run even, each dent planished by the coppersmith himself. The orchard is the bright kettle the smith raises. The comet is the fire that anneals the copper soft. The bridge is the well the kettle is filled from. A forger must planish 14 dents even, raise 14 dents and true 14 dents, an afternoon at the stake for a kettle that still leaks at the seam.
